lines.say: Half your warranty money? The store keeps it.

lines.text: Consumer Reports: stores keep 50% or more of the warranty price, way more than on the product.
lines.say: Consumer Reports says stores keep half or more of the warranty price. That's way more than they make on the product.

scene.label: Share of warranty price stores keep

lines.text: The trick is the claim rate. In one study, products failed about 5% of the time.
lines.say: The trick is the claim rate. In one big study, the products failed only about five percent of the time.

scene.label: How often products failed
scene.sub: Abito & Salant, Review of Economic Studies, 2019

lines.text: But buyers acted like it was 13%.
lines.say: But buyers acted like it was thirteen percent, paying for risk that mostly wasn't there.

lines.text: Say an $80 plan covers a $300 repair. 5% x $300 = $15 expected payout.
lines.say: Here's the math. Say an eighty dollar plan covers a three hundred dollar repair. Five percent of three hundred is fifteen dollars.

lines.text: Even at 13%, the payout is $39. On average, the seller keeps $65 of $80, before costs.
lines.say: Even at thirteen percent, it's only thirty-nine dollars. On average, the seller keeps sixty-five of the eighty, before costs.

lines.text: Same with cars: 55% of extended car warranty buyers never used theirs (Consumer Reports, 2014).
lines.say: Same with cars. In a twenty fourteen Consumer Reports survey, fifty-five percent of extended car warranty buyers never used theirs.

scene.label: Car warranty buyers who never used it

lines.text: If buyers knew the real odds, the study estimated warranty profits would fall over 90%.
lines.say: And if buyers knew the real odds, the study estimated warranty profits would fall more than ninety percent.

scene.label: Warranty profits if buyers knew the odds
scene.sub: Abito & Salant, Review of Economic Studies, 2019

lines.text: The business isn't fixing things. It's selling peace of mind, priced on your worry.
lines.say: So the business isn't really fixing things. It's selling peace of mind, priced on how much you worry.

lines.text: That's the money. Follow for more.

post.title: How extended warranties really make money
post.ig:
Half your warranty money? The store keeps it.
Consumer Reports says stores keep 50% or more of what they charge for extended warranties.
In one study, products failed about 5% of the time, but buyers acted like it was 13%.
The math: 5% x a $300 repair = $15 expected payout on an $80 plan. Even at 13%, it's $39.
Sources: Consumer Reports; Abito & Salant, Review of Economic Studies (2019).
News and education, not financial advice.
